articles.title: The 5 requirements a man must meet to win Sophie Cunningham's heart: “I have very high expectations for my future husband”
articles.standfirst: After shutting down a viral social media hoax claiming she prefers shorter men, the 6-foot-1 WNBA guard laid out the exact standards a future partner must clear
articles.summary: After shutting down a viral social media hoax claiming she prefers shorter men, the 6-foot-1 WNBA guard laid out the exact standards a future partner must clear
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has watched her profile skyrocket during her two seasons with the Indiana Fever , evolving from a gritty perimeter threat into one of women’s basketball’s most recognizable personalities.

Whether she is knocking down catch-and-shoot three-pointers, holding down the co-host chair on her Show Me Something podcast, or commanding millions of views on social media, the 6-foot-1 guard rarely minces words.

That candid streak was on full display earlier this week when Cunningham stepped in to squash a fabricated dating rumor.

On Tuesday, an Instagram page named Sport Pump published a graphic attributing a phony quote to the WNBA veteran: “I only date short guys, as I like them to look up to me,” the post falsely claimed. In the accompanying caption, the account joked that “short kings are having a field day” with the supposed remark while tucking in a disclaimer noting that “the quote is unverified.”

Cunningham spotted the post and dismantled it in two words. “Fake news,” she wrote directly in the comments section.

While there are no confirmed reports regarding her current relationship status, and she has noted she is single, Cunningham used a cover interview with Maxim to clarify what she actually looks for in a life partner.

Far from compromising on her standards, Cunningham admitted she holds prospective suitors to a strict bar: “I have a very high standard for my future husband.”

Breaking down the five non-negotiables on Sophie Cunningham’s marriage checklist

During her Maxim feature, Cunningham outlined five core qualities a man must possess to earn a spot in her future:

- A frame taller than 6-foot-1: Directly contradicting the viral Instagram hoax, Cunningham confirmed that height is an absolute dealbreaker. When asked whether her spouse truly needs to tower over her, she didn't hesitate. “Yeah, I think so,” Cunningham said. “I’m already so tall. The last thing I wanna do is bend down to kiss my husband goodnight. No, thanks.”

- A Christ-centered faith: Spiritual alignment sits at the very top of her list. Cunningham explained that she wants a partner who shares her Christian beliefs and can provide spiritual leadership. “He’ll be someone who is Christ-centered and can lead me in my walk with Jesus,” she said, adding that she hopes to find someone who will “push me in my faith”.

- Confidence, warmth, and emotional security: Navigating the nonstop scrutiny of professional sports, podcasting, and viral fame requires thick skin. Cunningham emphasized that her future husband must be “friendly, confident, and secure,” someone comfortable in his own skin who can handle the public spotlight while matching her quick sense of humor.

- An athletic lifestyle: Having spent her entire life competing at an elite level, Cunningham noted that she wants a partner who is “athletic” and shares an appreciation for staying active.

- Fierce loyalty and aligned morals: Above surface-level traits, Cunningham is searching for character. She stated that her ideal match is “just a good human with similar morals and values,” someone who is deeply “loyal” and “loves every little piece of me” as she looks ahead to one day settling down with children and a traditional home life.

Off the dating front, the eight-year veteran is entering an equally consequential chapter in her basketball career. Following six seasons with the Phoenix Mercury and two campaigns in Indianapolis, Cunningham is poised to become an unrestricted free agent now that her one-year contract with the Fever has expired.

Across 43 appearances during the 2026 WNBA season, she averaged 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.2 assists per game while shooting a crisp 46.0 percent from the floor and 41.9 percent from three-point territory.

Her combination of perimeter accuracy, physical defense, and veteran poise guarantees strong interest around the league this winter.

Whether she ultimately re-signs with Indiana or suits up for a new franchise next spring, any man hoping to win her heart off the court now knows the exact checklist he has to pass.

articles.title: WNBA analyst calls out Caitlin Clark as reason for Kelsey Mitchell leaving Indiana Fever
articles.standfirst: The veteran guard is approaching free agency
articles.summary: The veteran guard is approaching free agency
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever have one of the WNBA 's most productive backcourts, but the partnership between Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell is now attracting questions about whether individual recognition could become a factor in keeping them together.

Mitchell is approaching unrestricted free agency after completing her ninth season in Indiana, having established herself as the franchise's leading scorer long before Clark arrived as the first overall draft pick in 2024.

Despite producing a career-best campaign in 2026, Mitchell faces uncertainty over her Indiana future, with former ESPN presenter Cari Champion suggesting Clark 's enormous popularity could complicate the veteran guard's decision.

Speaking on the Flagrant and Funny podcast, Champion questioned whether Mitchell receives sufficient recognition for her accomplishments while playing alongside one of basketball's most recognizable personalities.

“I think the question is, does she feel appreciated, not necessarily by the fans, but is it hard to play in someone else’s light when you are arguably a better player than they are?” Champion said.

Mitchell has been a central figure in the Fever 's rebuilding process since arriving as the second overall pick in the 2018 WNBA Draft.

She led Indiana in scoring during seven of her first eight seasons, remaining productive even as the franchise endured several difficult years without reaching the playoffs.

Her partnership with Clark subsequently helped transform Indiana's offense, with the younger guard taking responsibility for much of the playmaking while Mitchell continued developing into an exceptional scorer.

The 31-year-old averaged 24.7 points in 2026, finishing with a WNBA-record 1,086 points while converting 135 three-pointers at a 45 percent success rate.

Champion nevertheless questioned whether those achievements would receive equal recognition if Indiana eventually won a championship.

“I know if she wins a chip with Caitlin Clark, she’s going to be integral, if not the most important player,” Champion explained. “And do you want to be Caitlin Clark’s team?”

She added that the attention surrounding Clark could result in the team's accomplishments being remembered primarily through the younger star's achievements.

Mitchell's comments add uncertainty

Mitchell has previously acknowledged the emotional challenges of playing in Indiana, particularly the criticism directed at players via social media.

“If I showed y’all my DMs about the hate and all of the stuff that comes with being a professional athlete, but specifically being an Indiana Fever basketball player, it’s a lot that goes into that,” she said during her exit interview. “And those days are hard as hell, man.”

Her subsequent Instagram activity fueled further speculation, although Mitchell later explained that she regularly publishes reflective messages following each season.

Clark has publicly supported her teammate's return, describing Mitchell as someone who has consistently supported her and emphasizing her importance to the Fever.

Meanwhile, ESPN personality Linda Cohn expressed doubts about whether Mitchell will remain in Indiana.

“My gut still says Kelsey Mitchell is a goner,” Cohn said.

That said, recent speculation highlights the difficult balance between individual recognition and collective success as Indiana prepares for a crucial free agency period.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham throws her hat in the ring to become the next Bond girl after receiving a glowing endorsement
articles.standfirst: The WNBA star is already making moves outside the basketball court, and a new opportunity has caught her attention
articles.summary: The WNBA star is already making moves outside the basketball court, and a new opportunity has caught her attention
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has continued to expand her public profile beyond her career in basketball, taking on opportunities in modeling and entertainment. Her growing presence at major events has also helped her attract attention from audiences who might not necessarily follow the WNBA.

The free agent guard recently appeared at the NASCAR Cup Series Championship Race at Homestead-Miami Speedway, where she served as Grand Marshal. She has also worked with Sports Illustrated Swimsuit and appeared in a Maxim photoshoot, adding to her growing list of off-court projects.

Riley Gaines puts Cunningham forward for a major Hollywood role

Her latest appearance caught the attention of former NCAA swimmer Riley Gaines, who believes Cunningham could be a strong candidate for one of Hollywood's most recognizable roles.

Gaines publicly nominated the basketball player to become the next Bond girl , an endorsement that Cunningham welcomed. However, the suggestion quickly divided users on X, with many believing the nomination was a stretch given that the Fever guard has no professional acting experience.

Others pointed to the competition, arguing that actresses such as Zendaya, Florence Pugh, Margaret Qualley, Sydney Sweeney, Anya Taylor-Joy and Chase Infiniti have considerably more star power and acting experience. Some also suggested that, with the exception of Sweeney, these names have considerably less controversial public profiles than Cunningham.

The criticism was directed at both Gaines and Cunningham . Some users mocked the basketball player's chances with comments suggesting she would need to be able to shoot to secure the role , a reference to her sport and her current status as a WNBA free agent. Others took a different approach, creating AI-generated images of Cunningham as a Bond girl to play along with the idea.

Cunningham is exploring opportunities beyond the WNBA

The search for the next Bond girl is expected to attract plenty of attention as the new James Bond production moves forward under director Denis Villeneuve . With the franchise preparing for a new chapter, audiences will be watching closely to see who ultimately gets the role , a decision that could make headlines around the world and set the tone for the next era of the iconic spy series.

While there is no indication that Cunningham is being considered by the productio n, she has previously spoken about exploring different career paths outside basketball. In an interview, she mentioned an interest in sports commentary, launching her own podcast and potentially pursuing coaching . She even admitted that becoming W NBA commissioner is something she could see herself doing , leaving several possibilities open for her next chapter.

articles.title: Kelsey Mitchell gets honest about Caitlin Clark era and Indiana Fever fan backlash
articles.standfirst: Kelsey Mitchell addressed the backlash from Indiana Fever fans and revealed how Caitlin Clark has supported her through the toughest moments.
articles.summary: Kelsey Mitchell addressed the backlash from Indiana Fever fans and revealed how Caitlin Clark has supported her through the toughest moments.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever have become one of the most high-profile teams in the WNBA , and with Caitlin Clark leading the way, the constant media spotlight could easily become a distraction. That hasn’t been the case for Kelsey Mitchell .

Over nine seasons, Mitchell has built a historic career in Indiana. She refuses to let the presence of one of the planet’s most famous athletes — or the noise that comes with it throw her off course.

The guard has established herself as one of the franchise’s cornerstone players. She has rewritten scoring records, earned recognition among the WNBA’s elite, and played a central role in transforming the Fever into one of the league’s most popular teams alongside Clark.

“I can only go by what I can control,” Mitchell told Heavy . “A lot of the stuff that you just mentioned is just literally out of my control.”

Her mindset is straightforward, even if maintaining it under pressure is not always easy.

“I can’t change how people see or feel about me,” Mitchell said.

Caitlin Clark defends Kelsey Mitchell against criticism

Clark’s arrival turned the Fever into one of the most closely watched teams in sports, but it also placed Mitchell and her teammates under a level of scrutiny rarely seen in the WNBA.

That pressure surfaced during her season-ending interview on October 3 , when Mitchell discussed the hate messages she received and the challenge of playing in front of fans who don’t always fully recognize her impact on the team.

Clark publicly defended her teammate and condemned the racist comments directed at Mitchell.

“As her teammate, it makes you upset because you care about your teammates so much,” Clark said during her exit interview.

The conversation resurfaced on November 16 after Mitchell posted an Instagram message about believing in herself despite external criticism. Some Fever fans interpreted the post as a possible farewell ahead of free agency, while others rushed to defend Mitchell’s legacy and importance to the franchise.

Mitchell later clarified that the message was a personal reflection on her season, not an announcement about her future.

In 2026 , Mitchell delivered the best season of her career, averaging 24.7 points per game and setting WNBA single-season records with 1,086 points and 135 three-pointers . Alongside Clark, she also made history as part of the first Fever duo to earn All-WNBA First Team honors in the same season.

articles.title: Angel Reese gets a surprise message from the Atlanta Dream after one year with the team
articles.standfirst: The move to a new city has brought a different chapter to the WNBA star's career
articles.summary: The move to a new city has brought a different chapter to the WNBA star's career
articles.body:
Angel Reese has experienced significant changes since leaving the Chicago Sky , where her frustration was sometimes difficult to hide. Her arrival in Atlanta, however, h as been accompanied by a noticeably more subtle attitude, while her performances on the court have continued to speak for themselves .

The 2026 campaign proved to be an important one for the forward , who quickly established herself as one of the Dream's most influential players. Her impact became particularly evident during the team's postseason run , when s he played a major role in helping Atlanta reach the WNBA Finals.

Atlanta Dream celebrates Angel Reese's first season

One year after joining the organization, t he Atlanta Dream took a moment to recognize Reese's contributions . The franchise shared a collection of her best moments from the 2026 season on social media, c elebrating the memories created during her first campaign in Atlanta with a special message dedicated to the player.

The recognition came after Reese delivered career-best numbers, averaging 16.4 points per game, alongside a league-leading 12.1 rebounds and 1.8 steals . Her performances also earned her the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year award, further highlighting how important she became to the team's success.

Angel Reese finds a fresh start in Atlanta

Although the Dream ultimately fell short of winning the championship against the Golden State Valkyries, Reese's presence throughout the Finals demonstrated just how valuable she had become to the franchise. She averaged 14.7 points and 12.9 rebounds during the seven-game series, adding 1.3 steals and 1.3 blocks per contest.

It would be hasty to suggest that Atlanta has completely figured out how to get the best out of Reese, but her first-year performances and game-changing presence during the Finals suggest that the move has worked remarkably well . Following the championship loss, the three-time All-Star also announced plans to step away from the spotlight during the offseason, focusing on herself and preparing for another title opportunity. With her contract keeping her in Atlanta through 2027, Reese has an opportunity to build on what she started , while the Dream's latest recognition serves as a reminder of what s he brought to the organization in just one year.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s “Ice Cold” Nike “Caitlin 1” gets an early release at an Indiana event collecting shoes for families in need
articles.standfirst: The limited early release gives some fans a chance to get Caitlin Clark’s new colorway before its wider launch next week
articles.summary: The limited early release gives some fans a chance to get Caitlin Clark’s new colorway before its wider launch next week
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark’s “Ice Cold” Nike “Caitlin 1” will be available before its wider release at an Indiana girls’ basketball event that is also collecting shoes for families in need. Hibbett announced that a limited number of pairs will be available for purchase at Brownsburg High School on Saturday, Nov. 21, during "Girls Sneakers 4 Santa". Attendees can bring new or gently used shoes to donate.

The early access is part of the event, which brings high school girls’ basketball teams together in Brownsburg. The school’s schedule lists the first junior varsity game for 10:30 a.m. Eastern time, matching the 9:30 a.m. CT sale time in the announcement.

The "Caitlin 1" “Ice Cold” is set for a wider release on Nov. 24 at $140. The colorway pairs a white upper with Racer Blue accents and a translucent blue outsole. It uses the same performance design as the "Caitlin 1’s" other editions; Nike’s product details do not list a new technology exclusive to “Ice Cold.”

What makes the “Caitlin 1” different

Nike designed Clark’s first signature shoe around three goals: a quicker first step, a faster step-back and a quicker shot release. Its standout feature is the Nike Opticast upper, a lightweight cast-polyurethane construction with raised details. Nike says the design is meant to reduce drag and support lateral movement; the "Caitlin 1" is the first Nike shoe to use Opticast.

Underfoot, a forefoot Air Zoom Turbo unit works with Cushlon foam through the midsole. A plate in the midfoot adds stability for pivots and changes of direction, while the rubber outsole uses a “C”-inspired traction pattern.

Clark’s personal details include “CC” and “22” markings and the phrases “Shoot More Threes” and “From Anywhere.”

The closest comparison within Nike is Sabrina Ionescu’s signature line. The Sabrina 3 and "Caitlin 1" both pair forefoot Air Zoom with Cushlon; the Sabrina 4 adds a TPU Flyplate and retails for $145, compared with $140 for the Caitlin 1.

The "Caitlin 1" also shares some underfoot elements with the Kobe 6 Protro, including forefoot Zoom and Cushlon. Its distinct pitch is the Opticast upper and a design focused on quick cuts, step-backs and perimeter shooting.

Caitlin Clark is helping bring women’s signature basketball shoes into a bigger spotlight. The interest around her Caitlin 1 gives Nike a chance to build on her influence with new colorways and special releases. For young fans, it also means seeing a woman’s game and identity take center stage in sneaker culture.

The interest around her Caitlin 1 gives Nike a chance to build on her influence with new colorways and special releases. For young fans, it also means seeing a woman’s game and identity take center stage in sneaker culture.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham goes off after two female influencers leave little to the imagination at NBA game
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever guard reacted after Brittany Renner and Celina Powell’s courtside outfits drew attention
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever guard reacted after Brittany Renner and Celina Powell’s courtside outfits drew attention
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Clippers’ 113-112 win over the Oklahoma City Thunder on Nov. 13 gave the struggling home team a much-needed lift. But the result wasn’t the only thing drawing attention at Intuit Dome: social media personalities Brittany Renner and Celina Powell went viral after appearing courtside in matching black mini dresses.

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham weighed in during a recent episode of her No Hesitation podcast with trainer Drew Hanlen. While reacting to the outfits, the WNBA player said she wanted to be respectful, then bluntly added: “Put on some damn clothes.” She also pointed to the children she said were sitting nearby.

Cunningham’s criticism sparked a wider debate

Cunningham’s comments focused on whether the outfits were appropriate for a basketball game with families in attendance. Another sports commentator, Jason Whitlock, put the responsibility on the Clippers, arguing that arena staff should not have allowed the pair inside dressed that way. His remarks shifted the discussion from the influencers’ clothing to the venue’s role in setting standards.

The NBA’s Fan Code of Conduct and Intuit Dome’s venue guide prohibit obscene or indecent messages on clothing , but the published rules do not spell out a specific dress standard for how much skin fans can show. The guidelines also give arena staff discretion in matters that could affect public safety or an event.

Renner and Powell are also the stars of Zeus Network’s Toxic Twins. The duo’s courtside appearance came just days before the show’s premiere, and Zeus CEO Lemuel Plummer shared video of their entrance. That connection drew attention to the series, though the available reporting does not establish that their appearance was a planned promotional stunt.

Sophie Cunningham’s reaction brought a woman’s voice from inside basketball into the debate over how other women show up at the game.

Her blunt criticism turned a viral courtside moment into a wider conversation about fashion, visibility and expectations in a family arena.

articles.title: “A huge lack of respect”: Basketball fans mercilessly mock the comparison between Sophie Cunningham and Dennis Rodman
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever guard's growing popularity has sparked an unexpected debate about one of basketball's greatest personalities
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever guard's growing popularity has sparked an unexpected debate about one of basketball's greatest personalities
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham’s rise into one of the WNBA’s most talked-about personalities has prompted an unexpected comparison, but basketball fans aren’t convinced that Dennis Rodman is the right match.

Broadcaster Robin Lundberg raised the parallel while discussing the Indiana Fever guard’s growing profile on his YouTube channel.

He argued that Cunningham has become a superstar away from the court despite not producing superstar statistics, much like Rodman attracted enormous attention during his NBA career through his colorful public persona and headline-making appearances.

“I mean, she is everywhere. Absolutely everywhere. I don’t know if I’ve ever seen anything like Sophie Cunningham, where a player who’s not a superstar player is such a superstar outside of the game,” Lundberg said.

“Maybe Dennis Rodman is the best comparison. Now, he was a big-time impact player and a winning player on the Chicago Bulls, but joining the nWo, the NBA Finals, and Madonna and whatever else he was doing at that period of time.”

Cunningham enjoyed a particularly memorable season despite the Fever exiting in the first round of the playoffs. Her on-court production was relatively modest, averaging 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.2 assists across 43 regular-season games while playing 22.2 minutes per contest.

However, her popularity experienced a remarkable surge, with her Instagram following increasing from 1.4 million to approximately 4.3 million.

Her willingness to embrace the spotlight was evident when she publicly campaigned on X to become the next Bond girl opposite Robert Pattinson.

The post generated considerable attention and added another viral moment to a season already filled with memorable gestures and outspoken commentary.

Fans say Rodman’s legacy deserves more respect

Lundberg’s comparison quickly attracted criticism from basketball fans who felt it overlooked what Rodman had accomplished throughout his playing career.

One reaction described the analogy as “a huge lack of respect,” while others emphasized that Rodman was already an elite NBA player long before his celebrity status reached another level with the Chicago Bulls.

The former Detroit Pistons forward won two consecutive NBA championships with the franchise in 1989 and 1990. He also collected Defensive Player of the Year honors in 1990 and 1991, alongside five consecutive All-Defensive First Team selections.

His achievements eventually earned him a place in the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame, while Detroit retired his No. 10 jersey in recognition of his contributions.

Rodman subsequently added three more championships alongside Michael Jordan and Scottie Pippen in Chicago. His seven consecutive rebounding titles further demonstrate why many fans believe comparing his basketball legacy with Cunningham’s current accomplishments is unfair.

Cunningham has certainly established herself as a recognizable personality and surpassed 2,000 career WNBA points. Her 2025 résumé also includes a Commissioner’s Cup championship. However, she still has considerable ground to cover before matching Rodman’s remarkable collection of individual and team achievements.

Cunningham has captured enormous attention through her personality and off-court activities, while Rodman established himself as a championship-winning superstar through his performances before becoming an international celebrity. That explains why so many basketball fans weren't impressed with Lundberg’s assessment.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham leaves fans stunned with a different side of herself
articles.standfirst: The WNBA star trades the court for the camera in a Maxim photoshoot that showcases her fashion-forward and daring side.
articles.summary: The WNBA star trades the court for the camera in a Maxim photoshoot that showcases her fashion-forward and daring side.
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham is proving that the WNBA offseason is also a chance to explore passions beyond basketball . Away from the demands of competition, the basketball star has found time to step into the world of modeling, an experience that recently led her to take part in a photoshoot for Maxim.

The magazine unveiled a series of photos featuring Cunningham, with the outfits and details of each look quickly catching fans' attention. In one of the shots, Sophie wears a lingerie set paired with a long, sheer dark green robe featuring floral lace trim and wide sleeves .

The second look takes a completely different approach. This time, she wears a short black long-sleeved dress with metallic details at the cuffs . The outfit offers a striking contrast to the first look, highlighting another side of the photoshoot's style.

Modeling is also winning over the WNBA star

Her interest in fashion goes beyond this latest photoshoot. Through her outfit choices at various public appearances, Cunningham has shown her appreciation for current trends , while high-profile events and brand collaborations have given her even more opportunities to explore this side of her personality.

That connection between sports and fashion has even extended to footwear. One example is her Adidas Crazy Energy "Sophie Cunningham" PE , an exclusive player edition based on a basketball silhouette already featured in the brand's lineup.

Sophie Cunningham is showing that her personality and interests extend well beyond the basketball court, with fashion becoming another outlet for her to express herself and explore new opportunities. Now, fans will have to wait and see what other surprises she has in store.
